assertion_analysis.assertion: dispatch_pair raises CrewError for both the dry run and the real dispatch, the message contains 'Resolve with', candidate and candidate-model, no worker is launched and the run-dir name set is unchanged
assertion_analysis.falsified_by: removing _refuse_arms_that_resolve_alike from dispatch_pair - the negative control records exactly this (DID NOT RAISE CrewError, EXIT=1); a message naming a backend other than the one both arms resolved to would redden the PAIR_BACKEND-in-message assertion

assertion_analysis.assertion: a pair with the primary on the flight default pairs, its dry run reporting primary backend 'alpha' and shadow backend 'candidate' with model candidate-model
assertion_analysis.falsified_by: a code change that refused this pair, ignored pair_backend, or routed the shadow onto the primary's backend; the two sides are the returned result and independent constants, not the value passed in

assertion_analysis.assertion: a pair whose arms share the candidate backend but run different models pairs, with the primary model other-model and the shadow model candidate-model
assertion_analysis.falsified_by: dropping the model branch so the check fires on equal backends alone - the backends-only mutant fails this case (negative_control_backends_only.log EXIT=1), which also confirms the monkeypatched model substitution reaches the comparison

baseline_suite.revision_note: parent of the reviewed base; the pre-change arm

findings.text: the negative_control_note claims the backends-only mutation 'leaves that case green and fails the third case', but negative_control_backends_only.log shows 2 failed ids - the first case test_arms_that_resolve_alike_are_refused also fails, at tests/test_a_pair_never_runs_its_arms_alike.py:153 on 'assert CANDIDATE_MODEL in dry_message' - so the note contradicts the log it cites; state that the mutant reddens both cases and why.

the check infers 'models equal' from '"model" not in substituted', which holds only because the sole call site dispatch.py:814 passes configuration_overrides=(); a future caller passing an explicit model override would put 'model' in substituted even when both arms resolve to the same model and silently skip the refusal, so the coupling is latent rather than guarded.
